title: 5 Smallest Wild Cats on Earth 🐾
narration: Number 1 weighs under two pounds, lighter than a single bag of sugar. Yet it is a fierce apex hunter that stalks the wild forest. Starting at number 5, the oncilla. Found in the rainforests of South America, this spotted climber weighs only about five pounds. It has soft yellow fur and spends its life leaping between high tree branches. At number 4, the sand cat. This desert survivor weighs about six pounds. Thick fur covers its paws, protecting them from boiling desert sand as it hunts at night. In at number 3, the kodkod. Native to the forests of Chile, it weighs about five pounds. It is the smallest wild cat in the Americas and can climb straight down tree trunks like a squirrel. Number 2 is the black-footed cat. Africa's smallest cat weighs under four pounds. Do not let the tiny size fool you, because it has an astonishing sixty percent hunting success rate. And at number 1, the rusty-spotted cat. Weighing just about two pounds, it can comfortably fit inside the palm of your hand. It is the tiniest wild feline on the planet. Which of these tiny wild cats would you want to see in the wild?
